synopsis: Across the booklet, New Zealand incidents show that ordinary production tasks at tip heads and stockpiles can produce heavy-machine collisions, with reversing a recurring task phase [f15691, f3211]. The 2017 examples include dozer–777 truck and truck–dozer contacts, night-shift tip-head contact, and a stockpile-loading incident in which a loader bucket caught a reversing truck body and the loader overturned; reported consequences included tyre, rim and structural damage [f3557, f3229, f3345, f3569, f3264]. For October–December 2019, WorkSafe's vehicle-event breakdown was 46% overturning, 27% unintended movement or brake failure, 11% collision with other plant, 4% berm breach and 12% burst tyre [f3198]. This qualifies the broader finding that machine-to-machine and machine-to-light-vehicle near misses and damage collisions were the most frequently reported events across NSW, Queensland and New Zealand: plant collisions were not the leading category in that particular New Zealand quarter [f3583, f3585]. Frequency estimates remain uncertain because near misses were under-reported and the regulator warned that only a small fraction of quarry and alluvial operations had reported events in the preceding year [f3650, f3050, f11621].
